title: Focus and Dilution: The Multi-stage Learning Process of Attention
claim: Training proceeds through a repeating sequence of distinct stages, visible as plateaus and drops in the loss curve, with each stage explained by specific parameter dynamics.
layout: 3 regions: left data/architecture boxes, center loss curve, stage annotations around it
description: The figure has two parts. On the left are two stacked, color-bordered boxes. The red 'Data' box shows the Markov chain stationary distribution π, the transition matrix P, and a sequence S ~ P branching into three datasets S0, S1 and S2. These differ only in the final token, shown as sequences of numbers. The blue 'Architecture' box gives the attention formula and the model f_θ. The right part is a purple 'Phenomena' panel built around a central loss-versus-training-step plot. The plot has three curves for S0, S1 and S2, with dotted and dashed unigram and bigram baselines. Colored circles on the curves mark stage transitions. Around the plot are four stage labels in blue, green, orange and brown: Initial Condensation, Growth of Attention, Dilution of Attention, and New Direction of W0. Each label sits above short bullet points of parameter updates in math notation. The eye goes first to the loss curves and the colored stage headings.
caption: Overview of the setting and the focus–dilution training pattern. (Left) Sequences are generated by a Markov chain with stationary distribution π. We extract dataset S0, S1, S2 from the training set, which differ only in the identity of the final token in each sequence. (Right) The loss curves exhibit four stages: initial condensation, attention growth, attention dilution, and the emergence of a new direction.
abstract: Transformer-based models have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of domains, yet our understanding of their training dynamics remains limited. In this work, we identify a recurrent focus-dilution cycle in attention learning and provide a rigorous explanation in a one-layer Transformer setting for Markovian data via gradient-flow analysis. Using stage-wise linearization around critical points, we show that a single focus-dilution cycle can be decomposed into a sequence of distinct stages. First, embedding and projection rapidly condense to a rank-one structure, while attention parameters remain effectively frozen. Then, the attention parameters begin to increase, inducing a frequency-driven focus toward high-frequency tokens. As attention continues to evolve, it generates next-order perturbations in embeddings, leading to a mass-redistribution mechanism that progressively dilutes this focus. Finally, small asymmetries among low-frequency tokens lift a degenerate critical point, opening new embedding directions and initiating the next cycle. Experiments on synthetic Markovian data as well as WikiText and TinyStories corroborate the predicted stages and cyclical dynamics.
